mechanisms.name: Mover.Step (mover.go) — click gait / LOS carrot / plan follower
mechanisms.how: Trigger: every navWalk call. Ladder: click-gait at far carrots (game's own pathfinder, 1.6s rate limit), direct-LOS force-hold with fat-ray clearance, A*-plan farthest-visible-point carrot, thin-ray wall-hug escape, live->full planner flip at 5s stall / 12s orbit, then openBurst. Failure modes: MoveBlocked is dead code (bestAt reset immediately before the 30s check at mover.go:196-200), so the ladder's terminal rung never fires and outer watchdogs fire instead; planners and obstacle grids are rebound/rebuilt per call from navWalk.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the executor algorithm (movelab-measured: farthest-visible carrot, click gait, fat/thin ray distinction); REBUILD its ownership — it must be the only writer to the actuator, and its Blocked verdict must actually be reachable.

mechanisms.name: Navigator (nav.go) — clearance-inflated A* polyline follower
mechanisms.how: Plan once on inflated grid, string-pull to polyline, monotonic committed arc-length progress, visibility-clamped lookahead, path-conditioned stuck detection (2.5s), 32-direction straight-primitive localEscape. Failure mode observed: oscillation at pond collision 3 tiles from goal for whole runs — its 12-cross-track diverge and localEscape loop with no memory of having tried; its stuck clock is one of 7+ independent clocks over the same body.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the algorithm wholesale (it encodes real paid-for lessons: no per-tick replan, never regress, clearance-aware); subordinate its recovery to the single journey owner instead of returning Diverged into a caller that replans blindly.

mechanisms.name: navWalk wrapper (main.go ~4819)
mechanisms.how: Rebinds mover.live/full every call, rebuilds obstacle list (wedges + fenceWedges + colliding objects within 70) every tick, calls fightThrough on Blocked. Failure: obstacle set churns per tick without invalidating existing plans; fightThrough is unreachable via the dead MoveBlocked branch.
mechanisms.verdict: DISCARD as a wrapper; fold obstacle sourcing and combat-handoff into the movement authority proper.

mechanisms.name: Goto exit-seek (main.go ~7029-7349)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: curGoto != current area, no crossing candidates. mapExitTo translates map-frame exit to live coords; phantom-exit SQUARE-frame check (patched after run 15 burned 8,437 phantom rejections on the real Blood Moor->Cold Plains exit because a WxH box was the wrong shape under the axis-transpose); side-area escape via nearest adjacency; 40s best-dist watchdog -> frontier detour -> route abandon; entrance ritual (5s contact push / hover-spiral phases mod 9); ring search at radius 32 after 8s park; grid refresh every 4s; travel via navWalk.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the concepts (goal-progress clock, detour-then-abandon, hover-confirmed entrance ritual); DISCARD the implementation — five nested timers and phase counters living in loop-locals, transpose patched at the consumer instead of ingestion.

mechanisms.name: Crossing candidates + multi-hop BFS (main.go ~7005-7412)
mechanisms.how: BFS area graph for next hop; 3 candidates per border from live room graph; nearest-first pick with 60s failed-candidate sit-out (after round-robin marched 38 tiles west while standing 2 tiles from another crossing); 25s per-candidate timeout; final push-across with raw force-hold. Failure: candidate rotation and exit-seek are separate competing subsystems for the same journey.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP border-crossing via room graph + hop BFS; unify candidate selection with exit-seek under one journey state machine.

mechanisms.name: Town beeline session (main.go ~6934-6989)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: goto net-progress stall in town. Up to 6 chained 2s strides, moveStop-then-press per stride (key-edge law), ±26° sweep on no-gain, loop slept ~12.6s. History: single strides were stomped by the next tick's re-aim (2s out, 3s back, net zero — the literal fish) until sessions chained (469bbd0) and the key-edge discovery (2ea5d82).
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the stride primitive (release-aim-press, commit, re-read) as THE actuation verb; DISCARD sleep-the-loop commitment — commitment must be a journey property, not a blocking hack that freezes survival.

mechanisms.name: Town road waypoints (main.go ~6625-6653, ~6920-6932)
mechanisms.how: Hand-piloted measured waypoint chain to the gate (the mod's fences exist in no collision source). Two independent consumers (goto stall, corpse recovery) share one townRoadIdx cursor; road holds paced at 1.8s after 334 stuttering restarts from per-tick re-firing.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP as data — measured known-good paths are gold; store them in the atlas layer, give them one consumer.

mechanisms.name: walkToHold / moveStop key-state (main.go ~495-634)
mechanisms.how: Force-move as persistent held-key state with dead-man's-release timer; every non-walk input calls moveStop first. CONTRADICTION: its design premise ('force-move follows the cursor while held') was refuted by the key-edge law — a held key keeps the key-down direction regardless of re-aim; field movement worked only because churn creates constant edges.
mechanisms.verdict: DISCARD the held-key-with-re-aim model; rebuild the actuator on the stride primitive (edge per direction change) as the measured law dictates.

mechanisms.name: Global unstick rotating compass (main.go ~7449-7497)
mechanisms.how: Trigger: no 15-tile net progress for 2.5s (6s in nav mode). Rotates screen headings. History: spun at CPU speed after locomotion went non-blocking (13,807 lines / ~3ms apart in one Den pocket, 'running in circles by the stairs'), fought the Navigator causing the N/S running-around, needed pacing and nav-mode suppression patches.
mechanisms.verdict: DISCARD entirely — it is a second authority guessing blind; the journey owner's escalation replaces it.

mechanisms.name: Confinement break-out (main.go ~7415-7447)
mechanisms.how: 55-sample posHist; thin-strip span detection pushes toward walkable centroid with perpendicular jitter. Only active when navi==nil now.
mechanisms.verdict: DISCARD — vestigial pre-Navigator heuristic kept alive behind a condition.

mechanisms.name: openBurst clearance-scored escape (main.go ~4762-4794)
mechanisms.how: Samples live grid in 8 rays, walks the best two synchronously (sleeps the loop, because the async version got overwritten within ~10ms by the next tick's re-aim — 38 wedge stamps at one cell, position frozen).
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the read-the-room scoring; make it a maneuver the authority executes with real commitment, not a sleep.

mechanisms.name: Goto net-progress watchdog + wedge stamping (main.go ~6822-7003)
mechanisms.how: 5s fixed-window net-displacement check; on jitter verdict: entrance-zone standdown, fightThrough, pet-jam shove, else stamp refusal wedge + persist to atlas + beeline/burst. History: stamped false wedges from pet jams, combat preemption aging (resume-reset patches), town fences (town-stamp ban), own cell (poison escape hatch, 41 cascading wedges).
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP refusal-learning as a concept (actuation truth beats grid claims); REBUILD with cause classification — the system cannot keep learning lies and carving exceptions per lie.

mechanisms.name: Atlas (internal/game/atlas.go)
mechanisms.how: Persistent per-seed/area collision overlay; masked merge to loaded rooms only; sticky refusals; frontier query; 2-bit disk format with corruption-safe load. The one subsystem whose failure modes were designed for up front.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP as-is — the cartographer is the healthiest component in the stack.

mechanisms.name: mapNavi transpose scoring (main.go ~1578-1667)
mechanisms.how: Detects transposed map grids by scoring 4 flip variants against live collision (>0.65 agreement). Works — but the transpose is re-patched at every OTHER consumer (phantom-exit square frame, side-area bounds) instead of being fixed once.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the empirical variant-scoring; move it to a single grid-ingestion boundary so no downstream code ever sees an untransposed frame again.

mechanisms.name: Explore frontier commitment (main.go ~7790-7850)
mechanisms.how: Atlas frontier target, best-dist commitment clocks (12s), badDests memory, resume-reset for preemption aging. History: flat 25s re-pick let FrontierNear retarget to a frontier BEHIND mid-walk — literal back-and-forth.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP frontier-driven exploration; its commitment logic is a hand-rolled instance of the missing Journey abstraction — replace with the real thing.

mechanisms.name: Corpse recovery movement (main.go ~6581-6690)
mechanisms.how: Own stall detector (8s/3-tile), town-road holds, field last-mile chained strides (2×1600ms, sleeps loop), pack-strength retreat, 3min give-up / 10min cooldown. Duplicates goto's town escape and beeline machinery with separate state.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP the policy (don't feed the camp, give-up cooldown); DISCARD the duplicated locomotion — a corpse run is just a journey with a destination.

mechanisms.name: Combat locomotion (chase/kite/regroup/final-approach, main.go ~7534-8088)
mechanisms.how: Close-range straight pulses scaled by distance (<=30), long chase via navWalk with dest-drift tolerance, kite/regroup retreats via navWalk, contact override hands movement to combat (monsters aren't in collision grids). Blacklist-on-no-closing with army-engaged exemption.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP contact-override and posture concepts; route all its walking through the single authority so combat aims can't stomp travel state.

mechanisms.name: Entrance/stairs interaction ladder (main.go ~7152-7286)
mechanisms.how: Mapped-point steering with object-tile correction (map lies by ~7 tiles), contact push for walk-throughs, koolo's hover-spiral with UnitType confirmation, click fallback after 6s. History: 310 clicks never closing pre-contact-phase; ritual timers zeroed by bounce reflexes until the standdown zone.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP — hover-confirmed interaction is a measured law; but its phase timers must be owned by the journey, not ambient globals reset by rival watchdogs.

mechanisms.name: Global tick floor + per-branch sleeps
mechanisms.how: 80ms loop floor (added after unstick and loot spun at 3ms), plus ad-hoc 40/60/80ms sleeps after walk calls in individual branches. Cadence is tuned per call site, not owned anywhere.
mechanisms.verdict: DISCARD the ad-hoc sleep scatter; a scheduler with per-behavior cadence replaces whack-a-mole pacing.

mechanisms.name: Intent ledger claim() (main.go ~5347)
mechanisms.how: Priority+hold arbitration — but only loot/objects/combat use it; movement blocks compete via code order and bare continue statements.
mechanisms.verdict: KEEP and PROMOTE — extend the ledger to every tick-claiming behavior including all movement; it is the embryo of the missing arbiter.

rootDefects.defect: No single movement authority: the actuator (one held key + one cursor) is a shared mutable resource written by ~15 distinct code paths — Mover carrots, click gait, beeline strides, road holds, pet-jam shoves, entrance contact pushes, crossing push-across, close-range combat pulses, object approaches, chicken flee, unstick compass, breakout, openBurst — 87 direct walk/click call sites in main.go alone.
rootDefects.evidence: mover.go's own header declares 'One authority: behaviors declare destinations; the mover owns HOW', yet main.go bypasses it in every stall branch. Measured consequences: beeline strides stomped by the next tick's re-aim (net zero, 'the fish'); openBurst overwritten within ~10ms until made synchronous; unstick fighting the Navigator (N/S running-around).
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: Whoever runs last in the tick owns the direction. With N uncoordinated writers, back-and-forth is not a bug, it is the equilibrium: any two attractors (frontier behind vs exit ahead, candidate A vs B, escape vs re-aim) alternate at tick frequency. Every commit in the log that 'chained', 'paced', 'committed', or 'stood down' a behavior is a hand-carved truce between two writers — the architecture makes each truce necessary and none sufficient.

rootDefects.defect: No journey abstraction: movement intent is smeared across 40+ loop-local variables (gotoAim, exitSeekExit/BestDist/BestAt, exitDetourDest/Until, exitParkStart, exitRingIdx, exploreDest/Since/BestDist/BestAt, townRoadIdx, beelineFlip/LastPos, corpseWalkLastPos/MoveAt, roadHoldAt, gotoLastPos/ProgressAt, entranceContactStart, mapPointContactAt, exitClickTry, posHist, breakoutTick, progressPos/At, breakDir, lastGotoTickAt, lastExploreTickAt...) with no owner, no lifecycle, no completion semantics.
rootDefects.evidence: The resume-reset bug class: watchdog clocks aged while combat/loot owned ticks, so a 10s in-place fight read as a 10s wedge and stamped refusals on innocent ground (patched separately for goto, exit-seek, AND explore — three copies of the same fix). townRoadIdx is shared by two unrelated consumers. Area-change reset (main.go ~5903-5911) must remember to zero a dozen of these by hand.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: A journey ('get from A to B, then do X') is the natural unit of movement, with its own progress clock, escalation ladder, and completion. Without it, every behavior reimplements fragments of one — and the fragments desynchronize. The measured law 'every walk-at-target journey needs a progress clock' was implemented seven separate times because there was no single place to implement it once.

rootDefects.defect: Replanning without commitment: an 80ms stateless-reactive loop re-derives all intent every tick, so any maneuver needing duration must freeze the entire loop with sleeps (beeline session ~12.6s, road hold 2.1s, field strides 3.4s, openBurst 0.7s) — suspending survival checks, combat, and the death monitor while walking.
rootDefects.evidence: Commit a898889 'Commit to the stride: sleep the loop through beeline/road holds' — commitment was retrofitted AS blocking, the exact pattern the continuous-locomotion rewrite (walk/pause/walk at 40% duty cycle) was built to eliminate. The 334 stuttering road-hold restarts and the 2s-out/3s-back fence dance are both the loop stomping its own maneuvers.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: The loop has no vocabulary for 'this sub-goal owns locomotion for N ticks but higher-priority interrupts may preempt'. So commitment and reactivity are mutually exclusive, and the codebase oscillates between the two failure modes: stomping (reactive wins) or blindness (sleep wins).

rootDefects.defect: Seven-plus independent stall clocks with overlapping jurisdiction and no hierarchy: Navigator 2.5s along-path, Mover 5s physical + 12s orbit, goto 5s net-progress, exit-seek 40s best-dist, park 8s, candidate 25s, explore 12s, corpse 8s, global unstick 2.5/6s, confinement 55-sample — each empowered to seize the actuator when it fires.
rootDefects.evidence: Every major logged disaster is one watchdog misreading another subsystem's activity: bursts zeroing the entrance ritual's phase timer ('old code overriding us'), wedges stamped on pet jams and during combat preemption, unstick vs Navigator, the exit park timer reset by bounce excursions ('the bouncing WAS the fish'), 13,807 unstick firings at 3ms. Plus the Mover's own terminal MoveBlocked rung being dead code (mover.go:196-200) means escalation always leaks upward to cruder layers.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: Independent clocks over one shared body guarantee misattribution: no clock can distinguish 'I am stuck' from 'someone else is using the legs'. A single escalation ladder owned by the active journey — paused when preempted, advanced only by its own evidence — is the only structure that removes this class, and no amount of per-pair standdown patches converges to it.

rootDefects.defect: The core actuator contract contradicts the measured law it sits on: walkToHold holds the force-move key across re-aims on the premise that force-move follows the cursor, but the lab proved direction samples ONLY at the key-down edge (commit 2ea5d82) — a held key walks the original direction regardless of aim.
rootDefects.evidence: main.go ~591-598 comment: 'force-move follows the cursor while held... each walk call just re-aims'. main.go ~6973-6980 comment: 'a continuously-held key keeps the original (fence-facing) direction no matter where the cursor re-aims — six chained strides, moved=0. Field movement never noticed because combat/mover churn releases the key constantly, making an edge per carrot.'
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: The entire movement stack rests on an actuator whose steering works by ACCIDENT (incidental moveStop churn creating edges). Under a redesign that reduces churn — the very goal — steering would silently degrade. The stride (release->aim->press->commit) must be the ground-truth primitive, and everything above rebuilt on it.

rootDefects.defect: Collision truth is assembled per-consumer from four sources (partial live grid, sometimes-transposed map prior, persistent atlas, runtime wedges/fences + per-tick object stamps) with the axis-transpose disease patched independently at each consumption site instead of once at ingestion.
rootDefects.evidence: Run 15: 8,437 phantom-exit rejections of the area's own real exit because the phantom check used a WxH frame while the grid arrived transposed; fixed by a square-frame heuristic with ±50 slack (a shape-blind bandage, not a fix). mapNavi separately scores 4 flip variants. mapExitTo silently degenerates to delta=0 if alignArea ever mutates cached offsets (admitted in its own comment). SetObstacles copies whole grids on rebuild each replan.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: There is no single 'world model' component with one canonical frame, so every consumer must know about transposition, offset mutation, partial-vs-full coverage, and unknown-is-blocked semantics — and each one that forgets becomes a night of debugging. Frame normalization is a boundary concern; distributing it is the defect.

rootDefects.defect: Failure attribution is absent: the only learning signal is a binary 'passage refused' wedge stamp, with no classification of WHY movement failed (wall vs pet vs monster body-block vs combat preemption vs entrance ritual vs town fence) — so the system's only memory repeatedly poisoned its only map.
rootDefects.evidence: The accumulated exception list IS the evidence: never stamp in town, never stamp near pets, never stamp own cell (ClearRefusedNear escape hatch after 41 cascading wedges with playerWalkable=false), stand down inside entrance ritual zones, resume-reset after combat gaps. Each exception is a post-mortem for a false lesson persisted to the atlas.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: Learning from actuation truth is the right instinct, but a lesson without a cause is a lie waiting for a context change. The redesign needs the movement authority to know what it was doing and what else occupied the cell when refusal occurred — impossible while stall detection is ambient and diagnosis is a guess made by the stamping code.

rootDefects.defect: Behavior arbitration is code order + bare `continue`: ~30 blocks compete for the tick by position in an 8,000-line loop; the claim() intent ledger exists but covers only loot/objects/combat, and movement blocks (goto, explore, corpse, unstick, breakout) preempt each other implicitly.
rootDefects.evidence: The route-skip cascade: one pet-jam in the Den marched routeIdx from Den to Black Marsh in an hour while the character never left the cave — a stall in one block silently interpreted as completion by another. oppFight, trap gates, weapon gates, and posture hysteresis are all ad-hoc pairwise priority patches.
rootDefects.whyArchitectural: With no explicit arbiter there is no place to express 'travel owns this tick unless survival preempts', so every new behavior must know about every other behavior's guard conditions — O(N²) coupling that is exactly why the loop grew to 8,000 lines of interleaved carve-outs, and why the owner perceives the result as a fish rather than an intent.

keep: The measured laws, verbatim, as the actuation contract: direction samples at force-move key-down edge (stride = release->aim->press->commit); hover confirmation (HoverData.UnitID) before any click that must hit; panel clicks in raw physical pixels; world right-clicks work / panel right-clicks deaf; id=0 statics ignore synthetic clicks; town fences invisible to all collision sources; area grids may arrive axis-transposed
The Atlas (atlas.go) unchanged: masked room-rect merging, sticky refusals with presence-proof escape hatch, frontier queries, corruption-safe persistence — the healthiest subsystem in the stack
Navigator's core algorithm: plan-once on clearance-inflated grid, string-pulled polyline, monotonic committed arc-length progress, visibility-clamped lookahead, straight-primitive local escape

Mover's measured executor choices: farthest-visible-point carrot (0.98 path efficiency), click gait for far travel (the game's own pathfinder — 'the fish cure', retested post-DPI-fix), fat-ray vs thin-ray LOS distinction, wall-hug escape
Click gait as the primary far-travel mode, force-move strides for the last tiles and micro-steering
Room-graph border crossings + multi-hop area BFS for inter-area journeys
Hover-spiral entrance interaction (koolo's recipe: contact push for walk-throughs, UnitType-confirmed spiral clicks for the rest)
Measured town-road waypoint chains as data — generalized into 'recorded known-good paths' stored alongside the atlas
Contact override / fightThrough doctrine: monsters are not in collision data, so violence is a movement tool and combat postures (not walk-arounds) handle bodies in the way
openBurst's read-the-room ray scoring as an escape maneuver (under the single authority, with owned duration instead of loop sleeps)
Refusal-learning as a concept — actuation truth over grid claims — rebuilt with cause classification
The claim() intent ledger, promoted from a loot/combat sideshow to the arbiter every tick-claiming behavior (including all movement) must pass through
Goal-progress (best-dist-ever) watchdogs and detour-then-abandon escalation as the shape of journey-level stall handling — implemented ONCE in the journey owner
The transpose variant-scoring (mapNavi's 4-flip empirical alignment) — moved to a single grid-ingestion boundary
discard: walkToHold's held-key-with-cursor-re-aim actuator model — its premise is refuted by the key-edge law; rebuild all actuation on the stride primitive
All sleep-the-loop commitment (beeline sessions ~12.6s, road holds 2.1s, field last-mile 3.4s, synchronous openBurst) — replace with journey-owned tick leases that survival can still preempt

The global rotating-compass unstick, the posHist confinement breakout, and every per-path stall reimplementation (goto 5s net-progress, corpse 8s, explore 12s duplicates) — one escalation ladder owned by the active journey replaces all of them
navWalk as a wrapper (per-call planner rebinding, per-tick obstacle-list rebuild, grid copies per replan)
The phantom-exit square-frame heuristic and every other per-consumer transpose patch — normalize frames once at ingestion so no downstream code knows transposition exists
Uncaused wedge stamping and its exception pile (town ban, pet exemption, own-cell hatch, entrance standdown zones) — replaced by classified failure reports from the single authority
Duplicated town-escape/road/beeline machinery across goto and corpse recovery, including the shared townRoadIdx cursor
The 40+ ambient loop-local journey variables and hand-maintained area-change reset list
Behavior arbitration by code order and bare continue in a monolithic 8,000-line loop — an explicit arbiter with declared priorities replaces positional precedence
Ad-hoc per-branch cadence sleeps and the whack-a-mole tick-floor pattern — scheduling belongs to the loop, not to call sites
The Mover's internal dead escalation (unreachable MoveBlocked) and its private stall clocks once the journey owner exists — the executor executes, the journey judges
